history.origins: Vier-Anderle is a simple trick-taking tarock game suitable for gambling, played in the vicinity of Furtwangen in the Black Forest in Germany. A similar game is played in the region around Offenburg under the name Strassenwart. The rules were recorded by Nick Wedd, who learned the game from Walter Strunz. It belongs to the Rams group of trick-taking games and uses the Cego pack with pip cards removed.
timeline: Regional tradition: Played in Black Forest, especially around Furtwangen and Offenburg.
history.cultural: Black Forest regional tradition; also known as Strassenwart around Offenburg.
history.evolution: Simple Tarock gambling game derived from the Cego card tradition of Baden.

setup.deck: 38-card Cego pack. 22 tarocks (GstieÃŸ=highest to 1). Suits: Black K-Q-Kt-J, Red K-Q-Kt-J.
setup.dealing: The cards are dealt clockwise, with each player receiving four cards. Vorhand (the player on the dealer's left) leads to the first trick; the winner of each trick leads to the next.

rules.objective: Win at least one trick to avoid paying into the pot. When the pot has money, players may opt in or out; each trick won earns a quarter of the pot, and players who took part but won no tricks pay the full pot amount.
rules.gameplay: Follow suit. Must trump if void. Must head trick. Type 1 (empty pot): all play, win trick or pay pot value. Type 2 (pot has money): dealer adds 4 stakes, players opt in/out, each trick = Â¼ pot, no tricks = pay pot amount.
